text: One rainy afternoon, as a sudden squall lashed the Banjul foreshore, Erubami sought shelter beneath the gnarled roots of a towering silk-cotton tree near the shoreline.
In a hollow washed clean by the receding tide, his fingers touched something smooth and round.
He pulled free an ancient calabash, polished like dark amber and etched with geometric spirals that seemed to hum with silent warmth.
When he turned it over, three grains of golden rice fell into his palm, expanding instantly into a warm, fragrant loaf of bread.
